subject: Close runway resync — cadence ladder & procurement gating
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Lee <tlee@acme.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close runway check-in / MAP status

Hi Mateo,

Quick note — procurement put a hard stop on our signature window last night. They flagged three outstanding items in the security appendix and want the updated mutual action plan before they can move DocuSign to legal.

We’re still committed to the target go-live (Aug 21) but the procurement gating means our timeline will slip unless we get a concrete re-baselined MAP + decision ladder by EOD Wednesday. Can you share the updated MAP and a short mitigation proposal (credits, demo freeze, or incremental delivery) so we can make a case to procurement?

Tom (procurement) is on copy — he’ll confirm the exact gating checklist.

Thanks,
Sarah
Product Lead, Platform Integrations
Acme Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Tom Lee <tlee@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Close runway check-in / MAP status

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and quick context. I’ll put a tightened MAP and a short decision ladder together this afternoon.

Immediate proposal:
- Deliver updated MAP (two-week cadence) with explicit procurement acceptance gates.
- Offer a one-week pilot (reduced scope) to unblock go/no-go for production integration while procurement completes legal review.
- If procurement requires additional evidence, we can provide scoped audit artifacts and a short SOC2 excerpt.

I’m attaching MAP_v2.xlsx (draft) and a preliminary risk log; Marissa, can you add the cost/credit scenarios?

I’ll schedule a 30-min resync with procurement (Tom) and Sarah for tomorrow to confirm the gating checklist and commit on decision owners.

— Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- MAP_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, Tom Lee <tlee@acme.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close runway check-in / MAP status

Looping in quick risk framing and a couple of conditional options — see bullets below (pulled from the attached risk log):

Risk highlights (short):
- Procurement evidence delay (likelihood: medium) — impact: full acceptance window slip (~2–3 weeks).
- Integration acceptance ambiguity (likelihood: medium-high) — impact: partial go-live where some features remain behind a toggle.
- Pricing redline request (likelihood: low) — impact: negotiation time + approvals.

Contingency options (pick 1):
A) Pilot-first: Move a constrained pilot to Aug 2, allow procurement to finalize legal by Aug 21. Customer trades full go-live for earlier validation; Redwood provides 30% credit if full go-live delayed beyond Sep 1.
B) Canary fallback: Redwood ships high-priority endpoints behind a toggle on Aug 21; acceptance is feature-limited. No credits, but reduces customer-facing risk.
C) Procurement package: We assemble the SOC2 excerpts, KMS architecture note, and a short demo for legal. This can clear procurement in ~5 business days if nothing else blocks.

I recommend we propose Option C immediately (evidence package) + Option B as the operational fallback. If procurement pushes back, Option A should be our escalation (needs exec sign-off).

I’ve updated Close_Risk_Log_Q3.pdf with these options — attaching.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Close_Risk_Log_Q3.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Tom Lee <tlee@acme.com>

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement’s immediate asks (we will prioritize if you can provide):
1) Updated MAP that lists procurement acceptance as a named gate (owner + date).
2) DocuSign-ready contract with the security appendix updated to reflect the SOC2 evidence path (we don’t need the full SOC2 report, just the referenced artifacts).
3) A one-page mitigation letter from Redwood that explains the pilot option and associated credit mechanics.

If you can get 1–3 to me by EOD Thursday we’ll aim to move to legal review on Friday. I’ve started a DocuSign envelope and put a placeholder; link below when you have a final.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/ACME/Envelope/12345

Tom

Acme Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>

Tom / Sarah — summary and agreed next steps after our resync this morning: 

Decisions agreed:
- We will designate procurement acceptance as a hard MAP gate. Owner: Tom Lee. Target gate date: 2026-08-05.
- Redwood to provide a scoped evidence package (SOC2 excerpt + KMS note + short demo recording) by 2026-07-24 EOD.
- If procurement cannot clear by 2026-08-05, we’ll execute Canary fallback (feature-limited go-live) on 2026-08-21 as operational mitigation. Credit/financial escalation will be triggered only if full go-live slips past 2026-09-01.

Deliverables and owners:
- MAP_v2.xlsx (finalized) — Mateo (deliver by 2026-07-22 EOD) — attached.
- Close_Risk_Log_Q3.pdf (final risk framing + escalation ladder) — Marissa (delivered).
- DocuSign envelope: procurement will accept link once final contract is uploaded — Tom (procurement).

Next step: I’ll upload the finalized MAP and push the DocuSign-ready contract to the link Tom provided; Marissa will trigger the exec credit approval runbook if procurement signals a block. Priyom, please stand by on the credit ask — I may need a draft approval chain if we hit the Sep 1 credit trigger.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick collaboration.

— Mateo
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
